notes: Behavioral evals per the Agent Skills best-practices guide (three or more per skill). Fixtures live in scripts/tests/. Run each query in a fresh session with the plugin installed and judge against expected_behavior; there is no built-in runner — see evals/README.md.

evals.query: Turn scripts/tests/sample-notes/ into a service blueprint IR. Don't import anywhere yet.
expected_behavior: Scaffolds or detects a workspace before drafting (checks for blueprint-workspace.json)
Reads the ingest playbook before deep-reading sources; triages sources before reading at depth
Produces an IR that passes scripts/validate_ir.py with exit 0
Does not import or deploy anything — stops at drafted IR pending review/sign-off

evals.query: Import the signed-off IR into my Supabase project.
expected_behavior: Runs the §6 pre-flight: validator exit 0, per-scenario sign-off hash match, schema_version compatibility
Echoes the target project and waits for explicit confirmation before any write (wrong-project protection)
Never writes the service-role key to disk or chat; elevated writes go through user-run CLI or the connected Supabase MCP server's tools
On connector-unreachable, prompts a Claude Code reload rather than retrying

evals.query: Here's our FigJam board link — translate it into the blueprint app.
expected_behavior: Fetches the board per frame, never the whole board at once (token-limit rule)
Builds a crosswalk mapping (crosswalk-schema.json) before translating content
Flags unmappable lanes/columns to the user instead of inventing placements

evals.query: Audit the blueprint export at scripts/tests/sample-ir.json for gaps and jargon.
expected_behavior: Enumerates the check roster from skills/audit/references/check-*.md; every check is either dispatched or reported skipped-with-reason
Dispatches each executed check with only its own check doc (fresh-context auditor discipline)
Findings cite cells by key; wave-2 checks skip gracefully when spec columns are absent
Reports per-check counts; proposes no fixes

evals.query: Re-run the audit — we fixed the jargon in three cells since last time.
expected_behavior: Mints one new run_id for the run
Dedupes against prior findings per the playbook §3 table: open updates in place, dismissed stays dismissed, resolved reopens only on recurrence
Does not resurrect findings the user dismissed

evals.query: That channel-conflict finding about the phone lane is intentional — dismiss it.
expected_behavior: Routes to triage (status change), not a re-run
Sets the finding to dismissed with the user's reason attached
Leaves all other findings untouched

evals.query: Cut the customer's journey out of the imported blueprint as a slice.
expected_behavior: Reads the slice playbook, proposes the selection (cells by key) before writing prose
Every claim in the prose cites a cell key; nothing is invented beyond selected cells
Runs slice_tools.py validate before any import; validation failure blocks import

evals.query: We edited the cells behind the ops lane spec — regenerate that slice.
expected_behavior: Regenerates from current cells rather than editing stale prose
Preserves the slice's identity/key so the app updates in place
Re-validates before re-import

evals.query: Make the check-in moment slice into a storyboard.
expected_behavior: Runs the storyboard sub-flow only after the text slice exists
Uses skills/slice/references/storyboard-prompts.md for image prompts
Frame captions still cite cell keys

evals.query: What breaks if we remove the welcome call from onboarding?
expected_behavior: Builds a hypothetical variant; the database is never written during analysis
Walks leads_to/enables edges downstream (impact-tracer discipline: visited set, bounded depth)
Reports affected cells, broken assumptions, and where displaced demand lands, cited by cell key

evals.query: Should the refund approval step be customer-visible?
expected_behavior: Restages the moment across the visibility line rather than replaying the whole scenario
Weighs frontstage/backstage consequences using lane-roles semantics
Delivers a recommendation with cited cells, not a blueprint edit

evals.query: The team accepted the welcome-call analysis. Make it real.
expected_behavior: Emits a change request conforming to skills/whatif/references/change-request-schema.json
Hands off to the map skill's update flow for the actual edit + re-sign-off + re-import
Does not write blueprint tables directly from the whatif skill

evals.query: In onboarding, the kickoff call leads to the first quarterly review, which lives in the account-review scenario on its renewal path. What breaks if we drop the kickoff call?
expected_behavior: Traces the base export of the whole service, not only the onboarding scenario
Follows the leads_to edge into the account-review scenario and keeps walking there, under the same visited set and depth cap
Names the quarterly review's scenario and path beside its cell key (the tracer's reached_in field)
Brings the account-review scenario into scope: its sign-off hash is embedded with onboarding's in every artifact
